items.title: A Critical Analysis of AI from the Perspective of the Philosophy of Science among Grade X Students at SMA Don Bosco Padang
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) facilitates access to information in education, increasing the importance of critically evaluating claims and their underlying assumptions. This study examined Grade 10 students’ ability to distinguish facts, opinions, and values in AI-related information at SMA Don Bosco Padang from a philosophy of science perspective. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed involving 33 students. Data were collected through a 15-item written test comprising five items each for fact, opinion, and value identification. Descriptive analysis examined frequencies, percentages of correct responses, score distributions, and classification error patterns. Across 495 responses, 337 were correct and 158 were incorrect, yielding an overall accuracy of 68.08%. Accuracy was highest for opinion identification (76.36%), followed by fact identification (67.88%) and value identification (60.00%). Value identification presented the greatest difficulty, with an error rate of 40.00%. These findings reveal descriptive differences in students’ classification performance, particularly their greater difficulty recognizing values within AI-related information. From a philosophy of science perspective, the results underscore the relevance of epistemology for evaluating evidence and the justification of claims, alongside axiology for recognizing ethical considerations. The study provides contextual evidence to inform AI literacy instruction that integrates information verification, critical reasoning, and ethical reflection to support responsible technology use.

items.title: AI and Classroom Assessment in Pre-service Teacher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research Trends, Thematic Evolution, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Assessment preparation in teacher education remains a persistent concern as pre-service teachers are increasingly expected to design valid assessments, generate meaningful feedback, interpret learning evidence, and exercise professional judgment in AI-mediated classrooms. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of research on artificial intelligence-enhanced classroom assessment in pre-service teacher education from 2005 to 2025. Using Scopus-indexed publications, the study analyzed 344 documents from 242 sources to map publication trends, citation patterns, influential authors and institutions, geographic distribution, co-citation structures, keyword co-occurrence networks, and thematic evolution. Results show that the field is young but rapidly expanding, with an annual growth rate of 29.61% and a sharp increase in publications from 2022 onward, reflecting the growing influence of generative AI, ChatGPT, automated feedback, learning analytics, and intelligent learning systems. Co-citation analysis revealed three intellectual foundations: teacher knowledge and research foundations, generative AI-mediated pedagogical practice, formative feedback and automated assessment. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified four major thematic clusters: AI integration and ethical teacher education, intelligent learning systems and data-driven student learning, AI-supported feedback and personalization, and assessment analytics and evidence-based grading. The findings suggest that AI-enhanced classroom assessment is not merely a technological issue but a pedagogical and professional concern requiring assessment literacy, AI literacy, ethical judgment, and teacher agency. The study contributes a field-level understanding of this emerging research domain and highlights the need for more focused, ethical, and context-sensitive studies on how pre-service teachers design, evaluate, and use AI-supported classroom assessments.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Integration in Education: Teachers’ Utilization, Perceptions, and Implementation Challenges
items.abstract: This study explored the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in chemistry instruction, focusing on teachers’ utilization patterns, perceptions, and the challenges they encounter. A sample of 18 chemistry teachers from various institutions participated, providing insights into the types and frequency of AI tools used, including ChatGPT, ChemCollective, and PhET Interactive Simulations. Findings indicate that generative AI tools—particularly ChatGPT—are the most widely adopted due to their accessibility, versatility, and ease of integration. In contrast, subject-specific and creative AI platforms remain underutilized, suggesting that familiarity, perceived complexity, and awareness significantly influence adoption patterns. Teachers demonstrated strongly positive perceptions of AI integration in both curriculum and instruction, recognizing its potential to enhance content delivery, student engagement, personalized learning, and the development of 21st-century skills. No significant differences were found across institutions, indicating a shared readiness to integrate AI in chemistry education. Despite these favorable perceptions, effective implementation is constrained by technical limitations, infrastructure gaps, data quality concerns, usability challenges, ethical issues, and privacy risks. Teachers also expressed concerns about over-reliance on AI and the potential reduction of meaningful teacher–student interaction, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a balanced, human-centered approach. Overall, the findings support the strategic and guided adoption of AI as a pedagogical enhancement tool rather than a substitute for professional judgment and instructional expertise. The results highlight the need for structured, discipline-specific professional development that emphasizes prompt literacy, critical evaluation of AI outputs, ethical awareness, and pedagogical alignment. Strengthening technological infrastructure, establishing sustained institutional support systems, and developing clear guidelines for responsible AI use are essential to ensure effective, equitable, and ethically grounded integration of AI in chemistry education.

items.title: Cell IO: a database linking single-cell transcriptomes to literature-derived knowledge of cell functions and perturbations
items.abstract: Abstract Single-cell transcriptome databases tell us which genes a cell type expresses, but what a cell type does, and what happens to it when a gene is perturbed, remains scattered across the literature. Cell IO (https://cell-io.riken.jp/) links these two kinds of knowledge through Cell Ontology identifiers. Its transcriptome layer re-processes 10x Chromium single- cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq experiments of human, mouse, and rat from the Sequence Read Archive with a uniform pipeline, annotates clusters with Cell Ontology terms restricted by the tissue of origin, and stores the cell type composition and UMAP embedding of every experiment (currently 14,931 experiments and 82.9 million cells). Its literature layer holds 895,258 claims extracted with a large language model and verified in a second pass from open-access abstracts, review articles, and gene perturbation studies in immunology and neuroscience, each with the verbatim sentence, highlighted entity spans, evidence strength, and ontology-normalized cell, gene, and context. The web interface lets users search cell types by name, synonym, or identifier, find the experiments in which a cell type is most abundant, inspect the composition and embedding of each experiment, read and filter the claims about a cell type by knowledge base, direction, evidence strength, and organism, and identify cell types whose functional characterization is missing from part of the literature. Cell IO is freely available without registration.

items.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Temperature Control in Greenhouses: A DQN-Based Framework and Experimental Evaluation
items.abstract: Abstract The integration of artificial intelligence into controlled environment agriculture represents a transformative opportunity for addressing global food security challenges while promoting sustainable resource utilisation. This paper presents a comprehensive Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for optimizing greenhouse temperature management, leveraging data from the second edition of the Autonomous Greenhouse Challenge. We formulate the climate control problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and implement a Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent that learns to regulate temperature through discrete actions: heating, cooling, or maintaining the current state. Our methodology incorporates a sophisticated reward function that balances multiple objectives, including maintaining optimal growing conditions, minimizing energy consumption, and ensuring temperature stability. The agent is trained and evaluated on a subset of the 2019 challenge dataset, specifically utilizing measurements from the Reference team's compartment to ensure data consistency and reliability. Experimental results demonstrate that the RL agent effectively learns an adaptive control policy, achieving an average comfort zone occupancy of 40.1\% across diverse starting conditions while demonstrating appropriate action selection based on environmental state. The agent exhibits particularly strong performance when initialised within the optimal temperature range, achieving 100\% comfort zone occupancy in multiple evaluation episodes. This research contributes to the growing body of knowledge on AI-driven agricultural automation by providing a reproducible methodology, comprehensive performance analysis, and insights into the practical challenges of implementing RL systems in real-world greenhouse environments. The findings suggest that RL approaches offer a viable path toward autonomous greenhouse management with potential benefits for crop yield optimization and energy efficiency.

items.title: Human-AI Collaboration in Urban Digital Transformation: Balancing Efficiency and Human Values in Shanghai’s AI-Enabled Talent Recruitment
items.abstract: In the context of the urban digital revolution, recruitment through AI technologies has become common practice to address competition in the labor market. However, it is still unclear how the effectiveness of such recruitment is connected with humanistic values. For this research, an exploratory qualitative research design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with eight human resource professionals in Shanghai. Based on the results, the use of AI in recruitment led to increased efficiency mainly when screening candidates through high-volume, standardized processes, although the promised efficiency was not delivered in practice because the introduction of the AI system increased the workload. Patterns of human-machine cooperation were observed in different companies: tech companies and foreign companies are inclined to adopt interactive adjustment approaches, while state-owned enterprises retain human-dominated decision-making. Transparency of algorithms was still lacking in numerous instances, and there was an asymmetry in the accountability framework of algorithms, wherein disobeying algorithms carries more personal consequences than obeying them. The more experienced professionals became more autonomous in their work, while the less experienced professionals depended more on the algorithm. Issues like management support, information accuracy, and departmental integration have a major impact on implementation. This study contributes to the theory of human-machine collaboration by proposing the concept of asymmetric algorithmic accountability, which captures the uneven distribution of organizational consequences for following versus overriding AI recommendations and shapes practitioner behavior in ways that extend beyond individual trust or algorithmic transparency.

items.title: Human-AI Communication Symbiosis: How Educators Reconstruct Authority and Identity in the Algorithmic Era
items.abstract: The present schooling system is currently facing a dual disruptive crisis, spurred by the encroachment of social media algorithms and generative Artificial Intelligence (AI). While these forces impact the way students learn and think about information, they also induce an epistemological overhaul in the ecology of instructional communication. Students, with their visual rhetorical frameworks from digital platforms and the use of AI for analytical processing, present an apparent disciplinary crisis for their educators-a communication crisis in disguise. Applying Karl Weick's Sensemaking theory, this paper examines school leaders and Guidance Counselors in Samarinda, Indonesia's understanding of these ambiguities and reconceptualization of their roles. Through qualitative case studies based on teachers' pedagogical narratives, this study shows that teachers' epistemological authority is diminishing as they negotiate the hegemonic algorithmic communication. They respond to the students' fear of cognitive degradation by reorienting from a "knowledge transmitting" communicative practice towards "ethical verifiers" and "empathetic listeners." A Human-AI symbiosis is being created with the machine as information provider and humans as ethical validators and empathic listener. Implications were made for the development of policies related to algorithmic communication literacy and the application of tactical empathy in the classroom.

items.title: Hybrid Intelligence as a Tool for Textual Decoding: Integrating the Literary Detective Framework in Higher Education
items.abstract: This paper explores the transformative integration of Hybrid Intelligence (HI) within the landscape of higher philological education, specifically operationalized through the innovative 'Literary Detective' pedagogical framework. Amidst the shifting cognitive baselines of the digital era, this study addresses the crisis of sustained deep attention by proposing a synergistic model of textual archaeology. The research focuses on the intricate process of multidimensional decoding, wherein human cultural intuition collaborates with the computational power of Large Language Models (LLMs) to excavate latent intertextual layers across a diverse literary corpus.The study provides a comparative analysis of foundational and modern texts, demonstrating how a structured Decoding Matrix facilitates the identification of complex cultural codes in the cosmological epics of Vaja-Pshavela, the impressionistic prose of Niko Lortkipanidze, and the tragic war poetry of Mirza Gelovani, alongside the works of Homer, Margaret Atwood, and Ana Kalandadze. The findings reveal that Artificial Intelligence, when utilized as a cognitive scaffold rather than a replacement for authorial voice, significantly amplifies the student's capacity to navigate intertextual networks and resolve “artificial hallucinations” through intuitive filtering. Empirical evidence suggests that this hybrid approach not only increases the efficiency of thematic identification by approximately 38% but also fosters advanced critical thinking and digital literacy. Ultimately, the paper argues for a paradigm shift in the humanities, positioning the student as an active investigator in an AI-augmented hermeneutic environment, ensuring the continued relevance of philological rigor in a post-digital academic world.

items.title: INTEGRASI GENERATIVE VIDEO DALAM WORKFLOW PRODUKSI VFX FILM PENDEK “SPLIT//SECOND”
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative video technology presents novel opportunities for visual effects (VFX) asset generation, yet full reliance on artificial intelligence often creates visual inconsistencies, reduced artistic control, and integration barriers with live-action footage. This article aims to analyze the integration of generative video into the VFX post-production workflow of the short film “SPLIT//SECOND” and evaluate its effectiveness relative to conventional computer-generated imagery (CGI) practices. Employing a practice-based research methodology, the production applied a hybrid workflow where live-action footage serves as the physical reality anchor while artificial intelligence assets construct surreal virtual reality (VR) elements. Empirical results demonstrate that generative video substantially accelerates visual asset acquisition with up to 95% time efficiency, reducing manual tasks from 60–90 minutes to approximately 30 seconds to 3 minutes. Although it eliminates manual modeling labor, this method does not remove the essential requirements of digital compositing, rotoscoping, tracking, and color matching, while also introducing variable operating costs driven by platform credit consumption. ABSTRAK Perkembangan teknologi generative video membuka peluang baru dalam penyediaan aset visual effects (VFX), namun penggunaannya secara mandiri kerap memicu kendala konsistensi visual, penurunan kontrol artistik, dan hambatan integrasi dengan rekaman live-action. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis integrasi generative video dalam workflow produksi VFX pada film pendek “SPLIT//SECOND” serta membandingkan efektivitasnya dengan pendekatan computer-generated imagery (CGI) konvensional. Penciptaan karya menerapkan metode practice-based research melalui hybrid workflow yang menempatkan rekaman live-action sebagai jangkar realitas fisik dan elemen berbasis kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence / AI) sebagai pembangun dunia virtual reality (VR). Pengujian empiris membuktikan bahwa pemanfaatan generative video mampu mempercepat penyediaan aset visual secara signifikan dengan efisiensi waktu mencapai 95%, yakni dari durasi manual sekitar 60–90 menit menjadi hanya 30 detik hingga 3 menit. Kendati memangkas tahapan teknis permodelan manual, pendekatan ini tidak mengeliminasi kebutuhan digital compositing, rotoscoping, tracking, dan color matching, serta menimbulkan konsekuensi beban biaya variabel berbasis konsumsi credits.

items.title: Mapping gender, agency, and objectification in Arabic poetry: an ontology-guided computational study
items.abstract: Abstract Gender, agency, and objectification are important dimensions of how participants and relationships are represented in poetry, yet their systematic study in Arabic verse remains difficult because meaning is often conveyed through metaphor, ellipsis, compressed syntax, and context-dependent relations. This study investigates how gendered agency and objectification are represented across a large corpus of Arabic poetry and examines whether computational analysis can capture these literary-semantic relations while preserving textual evidence and interpretive uncertainty. A neuro-symbolic computational framework was developed to represent participants, events, agency, gender representation, and objectification as explicit, evidence-linked semantic relations. Large language model extraction was combined with formal constraint validation and expert adjudication. Evaluated against an expert-annotated sample of 4,500 verses, automated semantic extraction achieved an F1-score of 0.884 on the hold-out test set. Following evaluation and targeted adjudication within the annotated sample, the resulting constraint-guided pipeline was applied across 31,209 single-verse poems spanning twelve historical periods and eight poetic genres. Corpus-level analysis identified distinct distributions in gendered agency: male-coded participants were classified as active in 61.8\% of agency-related instances, compared with 48.2\% for female-coded participants, while the latter showed higher proportions of reactive and passive involvement. Objectification was distributed across multiple forms, with symbolic objectification emerging as the most frequent category (38.4\%), exceeding direct physical objectification (21.6\%). These results make recurrent patterns of gendered literary representation systematically inspectable at corpus scale while retaining links to textual evidence, ambiguity, and provenance. Ultimately, the study demonstrates how evidence-grounded computational methods can support large-scale investigation of literary representation while retaining interpretive boundaries.

items.title: PENGEMBANGAN COURSE TERINTEGRASI AI BERBASIS PROBLEM BASED LEARNING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KEMAMPUAN PENERAPAN PROSEDUR DAN PEMECAHAN MASALAH SISWA SMP
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Informatics education requires instructional designs that connect conceptual understanding with procedural application and contextual problem-solving. This study aimed to develop an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-integrated course based on Problem-Based Learning (PBL) to support these two competencies among junior high school students. The product was developed using the Moodle platform by combining digital learning materials, problem-based activities, and AI support in the form of explanations and learning-material summaries. The needs analysis involved 113 students, while the learning-outcome evaluation employed an experimental group and a control group, each consisting of 34 students, using pretests and posttests. The needs analysis revealed percentages of 23% for decomposition, 50% for pattern recognition, 35% for abstraction, and 44% for algorithms. In procedural application of computational thinking, the experimental group's mean score increased from 58.40 to 82.60, whereas the control group's mean score increased from 57.90 to 70.30. For contextual problem-solving, the experimental group's mean score increased from 56.80 to 83.10, while the control group's mean score rose from 57.20 to 71.40. Descriptively, the experimental group demonstrated greater improvement in both measured competencies. These findings indicate the potential of the developed AI-integrated PBL course to support Informatics learning; however, its statistical effectiveness must be confirmed through inferential testing. ABSTRAK Pembelajaran Informatika membutuhkan rancangan pembelajaran yang mampu menghubungkan pemahaman konsep dengan penerapan prosedur dan penyelesaian masalah kontekstual. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan course terintegrasi Artificial Intelligence (AI) berbasis Problem-Based Learning (PBL) untuk mendukung kedua kemampuan tersebut pada siswa SMP. Produk dikembangkan melalui platform Moodle dengan memadukan materi digital, aktivitas pemecahan masalah, serta dukungan AI berupa penjelasan dan rangkuman materi. Analisis kebutuhan melibatkan 113 siswa, sedangkan evaluasi hasil belajar menggunakan kelompok eksperimen dan kelompok kontrol, masing-masing terdiri atas 34 siswa, dengan pengukuran pretest dan posttest. Hasil analisis kebutuhan menunjukkan persentase kemampuan dekomposisi sebesar 23%, pengenalan pola 50%, abstraksi 35%, dan algoritma 44%. Pada kemampuan penerapan prosedur berpikir komputasional, rata-rata kelompok eksperimen meningkat dari 58,40 menjadi 82,60, sedangkan kelompok kontrol meningkat dari 57,90 menjadi 70,30. Pada kemampuan pemecahan masalah kontekstual, rata-rata kelompok eksperimen meningkat dari 56,80 menjadi 83,10, sementara kelompok kontrol meningkat dari 57,20 menjadi 71,40. Secara deskriptif, kelompok eksperimen menunjukkan peningkatan lebih besar pada kedua kemampuan yang diukur. Hasil ini mengindikasikan potensi course yang dikembangkan dalam mendukung pembelajaran Informatika, tetapi efektivitas statistiknya masih perlu dipastikan melalui pengujian inferensial.

items.title: Performance of AI Chatbots in Adult Reconstruction Education: A Comparative Evaluation Using AAOS ResStudy Questions.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly incorporated into orthopedic education, yet their ability to handle complex, clinically oriented questions remains unclear. This study evaluates the accuracy, response time, and citation reliability of contemporary AI chatbots when answering adult reconstruction questions from the AAOS ResStudy question bank. METHODS: Fifty-five multiple-choice adult reconstruction questions were extracted and categorized by anatomic region (hip vs. knee), concept (clinical presentation, prognosis, management), and AAOS-defined difficulty. Seven chatbots (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-4o, Gemini, Gemini Advanced, Claude, and Co-Pilot) were assessed. Accuracy, response time, and citation quality (existence and relevance) were recorded. Statistical analyses included chi-square testing, t-tests, Pearson correlation, one-way ANOVA, and Kruskal-Wallis testing (p<0.05). RESULTS: Overall chatbot accuracy was 67.5%. GPT-4o performed best (80%), outperforming AAOS members (75%), while Co-Pilot ranked second (70.9%). Accuracy varied by concept, with highest performance in Clinical Presentation (78.6%) and lowest in Prognosis (63.1%). Difficulty strongly influenced performance, with accuracy dropping from 84.7% on very easy questions to 45.4% on difficult ones. Average response time was 3.6 seconds, and no significant correlation existed between speed and accuracy. Among citation-producing chatbots, Co-Pilot achieved 100% citation existence and relevance. CONCLUSION: Modern AI chatbots demonstrate moderate overall accuracy on adult reconstruction questions, with GPT-4o exhibiting the strongest performance. While chatbots excel at descriptive orthopedic knowledge, they continue to struggle with applied reasoning tasks such as prognosis and management. These findings support their use as supplementary, rather than primary, learning tools. Improving citation reliability and reasoning capabilities may enhance future educational applications. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: IV, Cross-Sectional Comparative Analysis.

items.title: Precision Social Medicine: Bridging the Gap Between Social Care and Health Systems Integration
items.abstract: Health systems serving children have increasingly invested in social care initiatives, yet these programs frequently demonstrate inconsistent effectiveness and face challenges in sustainability and scalability. Precision social medicine (PSM) offers a framework for addressing this gap by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) models to match social care interventions to patients’ clinical and social context. This article presents a practical, 3-step approach for operationalizing PSM within health systems serving children. These steps are to (1) codefine precision in social care with patients and frontline staff, (2) translate that definition into an AI/ML-informed strategy for identifying risk and assigning services, and (3) test the approach in workflows before it impacts care. We highlight integrating such a framework using pediatric asthma as a case example, tailored for the pediatric hospitalist managing the transition from hospital to home.

items.title: The Effect of Generative AI and Gamification on Enhancing Students’ Motivation Based on the ARCS Model
items.abstract: High school biology learning is often hindered by abstract concepts and cognitive overload, leading to low student motivation. Although generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and gamification show instructional potential, their combined motivational effects remain underexplored. Grounded in the ARCS model, this study examined the impact of integrating ChatGPT-based GenAI and gamification on students’ Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction. A longitudinal quasi-experimental repeated measures design was conducted with 52 high school biology students over eight weeks. Motivation was measured at four time points using a validated ARCS questionnaire and analyzed with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results showed significant improvements across all ARCS dimensions from pre- to post-intervention (p < .001). Attention and relevance increased steadily, confidence improved in later stages, and satisfaction rose overall. Reported challenges included limited personalized AI feedback, competition-induced anxiety associated with leaderboard-based competition, and increased cognitive load resulting from complex AI-generated content. The findings indicate that GenAI-supported gamification can enhance motivation in biology learning when supported by careful pedagogical design.

items.title: «МАШИННОЕ ОБУЧЕНИЕ И ИСКУССТВЕННЫЙ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТ: НОВЫЙ ПОДХОД К ЭКОНОМЕТРИЧЕСКОМУ АНАЛИЗУ» ЭКОНОМЕТРИЧЕСКИЙ АНАЛИЗ И МАШИННОЕ ОБУЧЕНИЕ В ОЦЕНКЕ ВЛИЯНИЯ ЦИФРОВОЙ ТРАНСФОРМАЦИИ И ИСКУССТВЕННОГО ИНТЕЛЛЕКТА НА ESG-ПОКАЗАТЕЛИ УСТОЙЧИВОГО РАЗВИТИЯ
items.abstract: Исследование основано на практическом вопросе, с которым всё чаще сталкиваются органы государственного планирования в Центральной Азии: насколько надёжны линейные модели при оценке влияния цифровизации, искусственного интеллекта и факторов устойчивого развития и достаточна ли их предсказательная способность для описания реальных социально-экономических процессов? Для ответа на данный вопрос была сформирована сбалансированная панель данных по 34 развивающимся экономикам и экономикам переходного типа за 2012–2024 гг., включая пять стран Центральной Азии: Узбекистан, Казахстан, Кыргызстан, Таджикистан и Туркменистан. В исследовании использованы открытые базы данных Всемирного банка (World Development Indicators), Международного союза электросвязи (ICT Development Index), Всемирной организации интеллектуальной собственности (Global Innovation Index), а также рейтинги ESG Country Risk. На одном и том же массиве данных были построены две группы моделей. Первая основана на классической эконометрике панельных данных и включает сквозную регрессию методом наименьших квадратов (МНК), модель с фиксированными эффектами и модель со случайными эффектами. Вторая объединяет четыре алгоритма машинного обучения: Ridge и Lasso как регуляризованные линейные модели, а также Random Forest и Gradient Boosting как ансамблевые методы на основе деревьев решений. Качество моделей сравнивалось на отложенной 20%-ной тестовой выборке по трём метрикам: коэффициенту детерминации (R²), среднеквадратичной ошибке и средней абсолютной ошибке. Полученные результаты свидетельствуют о существенном преимуществе модели Gradient Boosting. Она объяснила 96,8% дисперсии ESG-индекса против 81,2% у обычной линейной регрессии, при этом ошибка прогноза сократилась более чем в два раза — с 5,18 до 2,14 пункта. Данное преимущество связано не только с подбором коэффициентов, но и с различиями в природе рассматриваемых моделей: алгоритмы на основе деревьев решений способны выявлять пороговые эффекты и взаимодействия между переменными, которые в линейной спецификации усредняются в рамках единой функциональной зависимости. Расчёт важности признаков показал, что готовность к использованию искусственного интеллекта и уровень цифровизации совместно формируют более половины объясняющей способности модели, опережая по значимости даже ВВП на душу населения. Отдельный раздел статьи посвящён Узбекистану, индекс цифровизации которого за тринадцать лет увеличился почти втрое. На основе полученных результатов сформулированы три практические рекомендации по совершенствованию национальной системы ESG-мониторинга. EN The study is based on a practical question that public planning authorities in Central Asia are increasingly facing: how reliable are linear models in assessing the impact of digitalization, artificial intelligence, and sustainable development factors, and is their predictive capacity sufficient to describe real socio-economic processes? To address this question, a balanced panel dataset covering 34 developing and transition economies for the period 2012–2024 was constructed, including five Central Asian countries: Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan. The study uses open data from the World Bank (World Development Indicators), the International Telecommunication Union (ICT Development Index), the World Intellectual Property Organization (Global Innovation Index), as well as ESG Country Risk ratings. Two groups of models were developed using the same dataset. The first is based on classical panel-data econometrics and includes pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) regression, a fixed-effects model, and a random-effects model. The second group combines four machine-learning algorithms: Ridge and Lasso as regularized linear models, as well as Random Forest and Gradient Boosting as ensemble methods based on decision trees. Model performance was compared on a 20% holdout test sample using three metrics: the coefficient of determination (R²), root mean squared error, and mean absolute error. The results demonstrate a substantial advantage of the Gradient Boosting model. It explained 96.8% of the variance in the ESG index compared with 81.2% for conventional linear regression, while the prediction error decreased by more than half, from 5.18 to 2.14 points. This advantage is associated not only with coefficient estimation but also with fundamental differences in the nature of the models: decision-tree-based algorithms are capable of identifying threshold effects and interactions among variables that are averaged within a single functional relationship in linear specifications. Feature-importance analysis showed that AI readiness and the level of digitalization jointly account for more than half of the model's explanatory power, exceeding even GDP per capita in importance. A separate section of the article focuses on Uzbekistan, whose digitalization index increased almost threefold over thirteen years. Based on the results obtained, three practical recommendations are formulated for improving the national ESG monitoring system. items.title: A Bibliometric Mapping of Airport Security: Research Trends, Thematic Structure, and Practical Implications
items.abstract: Abstract This study presents a bibliometric mapping of the academic literature on airport security, aiming to chart the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and collaboration patterns of the field and to translate these patterns into implications for security practitioners and policymakers. A total of 1,207 documents indexed in the Scopus database between 2010 and March 2025 were retrieved and analyzed using bibliometric mapping techniques implemented in VOSviewer. Co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, publication-trend, and subject-area analyses were conducted to identify the most influential authors, the dominant research themes, and the disciplinary distribution of the field. The co-authorship network revealed ten major clusters comprising 44 authors and 102 connections, with Adrian Schwaninger emerging as the most central author, reflecting a distinct human-factors research tradition alongside a fast-growing computer-vision tradition. The keyword co-occurrence analysis identified 49 keywords occurring at least six times among 3,062 unique keywords, with “airport security,” “security,” “deep learning,” and “aviation security” as the most frequent terms. Publication output rose markedly after 2019, driven mainly by research on deep learning, X-ray imaging, object detection, and threat-recognition systems. Engineering and computer science were the leading subject areas. Beyond mapping the field, the study translates these findings into concrete implications for airport security operators and regulators, and identifies underexplored themes—including passenger experience, policy design, and the integration of human-factors and automated-detection research—that merit further investigation.

items.title: A Comparative Study of Tokenization Efficiency in English, Hindi, Marathi and Romanized Hinglish Across OpenAI Tokenizer Generations
items.abstract: Large language models read text as small pieces called tokens. The number of tokens decides how much text fits in a model’s context window and how much a token-billed service charges. Recent studies show that Indian languages need many more tokens than English, and that Hinglish, which is Hindi written in English letters, creates its own tokenization problems. However, to our knowledge, Marathi, Hindi and several spellings of Hinglish have not been compared side by side as tokenizers have improved. We built 99 parallel sentences in English, Marathi, Hindi and three Hinglish spellings, and counted their tokens with four OpenAI tokenizer encodings, from older to newer. On the oldest encodings, Marathi and Hindi needed 7.4 and 7.6 times as many tokens as English. On the newest, o200k_base, they needed 1.80 and 1.54 times as many. Hinglish needed 1.8 to 2.2 times as many tokens on the oldest encodings and 1.5 to 1.9 times on the newest, so it was much cheaper than Hindi on older tokenizers but not on the newest. Different Hinglish spellings of the same sentence changed token counts by 26% to 31% on average. These results show that the cost of writing in Indian languages depends strongly on the tokenizer and on the script and spelling a user chooses. The data and code are available at https://github.com/samruddhibelsare-max/hinglsh_tokenization_study.

items.title: A Comparison of the Effectiveness of AI-Assisted Learning versus Conventional Media for Children
items.abstract: This study examined the comparative effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted learning and conventional instructional media among fourth- and fifth-grade elementary school students. Although AI is increasingly promoted as a means of personalizing instruction, empirical evidence directly comparing AI-based and conventional approaches at the elementary level remains limited. A quasi-experimental Pretest-Posttest Control Group Design was employed, involving 42 students in an AI-assisted experimental group and 42 students in a conventionally taught control group drawn from intact classrooms within the same school. Learning effectiveness was operationalized through normalized gain (N-Gain) scores derived from pretest and posttest achievement tests previously established as valid and reliable. Because the experimental group's N-Gain scores departed from a normal distribution, between-group differences were examined using the Mann-Whitney U test, complemented by Cohen's d to estimate practical significance. Results showed that although the two groups began with statistically equivalent pretest scores, the experimental group achieved a significantly higher N-Gain (M = 0.40, medium category) than the control group (M = 0.26, low category), U = 1190.500, p = .006, with a medium effect size (d = 0.551). These findings indicate that AI-assisted learning produced greater and more consistent improvement than conventional media among elementary learners. The study contributes empirical evidence to the underrepresented area of AI-supported elementary education and offers practical guidance for teachers, curriculum developers, and policymakers integrating AI into classroom instruction.

items.title: A Comprehensive Review of ANN-Driven Smart Learning Environments via Brain-Computer Interfacing
items.abstract: The contemporary educational landscape is undergoing a radical transition toward data-intensive, interactive paradigms characterized by the integration of sophisticated artificial intelligence and neurosensing technologies. This review examines the convergence of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) as a transformative force in the creation of "Smart Learning Rooms." By synthesizing current research on Electroencephalography (EEG)-based cognitive monitoring and neural network-driven adaptive systems, this paper delineates a novel conceptual framework for a closed loop pedagogical environment. The study explores the mechanics of real-time attention assessment, the categorization of student learning styles, and the prediction of academic trajectories using diverse ANN architectures, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and multi-layer perceptions. Furthermore, the analysis evaluates the efficacy of neurofeedback in enhancing focus and skill acquisition while addressing the technical, ethical, and socio-economic challenges inherent in the "neuro-digital divide." The proposed framework demonstrates how brain signal monitoring and neural computation can collaborate to personalize instructional pacing, improve engagement, and provide objective performance indicators. The ultimate objective is to provide a rigorous synthesis of the current state of neuro-education and offer a blueprint for the development of fully adaptive, brain-responsive instructional environments.

items.title: A CT Lesion Foundation Model for Non‐Invasive Assessment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Aggressiveness and Prediction of Recurrence Risk
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with high recurrence rates following curative resection. Accurate non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and recurrence risk is critical for surgical decision-making and postoperative surveillance, yet remains challenging with conventional imaging modalities. Here, we developed a CT lesion foundation model (LFM), trained via self-supervised learning on 32,120 generic lesion and 6,387 HCC-specific CT patches to capture transferable intra-lesional imaging phenotypes. Across one internal and two external validation cohorts, the sequentially pretrained LFM (LFM-Seq) achieved area under the curve values of 0.916, 0.846, and 0.920 for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment, and 0.833, 0.885 and 0.795 for pathological grade assessment. The model remained robust under scenarios of limited training data and tumor localization perturbations. Furthermore, LFM-Seq-derived risk scores stratified recurrence-free survival (RFS), yielding an externally validated C-index of 0.701, and remained independently associated with RFS after adjusting for clinicopathological factors. Exploratory biological interpretability analyses showed that LFM-Seq-derived risk phenotypes were associated with suppressed lymphocyte-related immune programs. These results suggest that CT lesion foundation models can support non-invasive and robust characterization of HCC aggressiveness, recurrence risk stratification and discovery of interpretable prognostic imaging biomarkers.

items.title: A Random Forest-Based AI Decision Support System for an Integrated Indonesian Civil Service Information System
items.abstract: Digital transformation in public administration increases the need for personnel information systems that can consolidate fragmented civil-service records and turn them into timely, transparent, and actionable decision support. This study developed SIPINTAR (Integrated, Adaptive, and Responsive Interactive Personnel Intelligence System), an artificial intelligence-based platform designed to integrate civil-service personnel information and support administrative decision-making within an Indonesian government institution. The study adopted a Research and Development approach and implemented the system through a Waterfall-based Software Development Life Cycle. Personnel data from multiple source systems, representing 5,320 civil servants and more than 42,000 historical records for 2019–2025, were integrated using Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) processes. The integrated data were then subjected to cleaning, transformation, feature engineering, and Random Forest modeling. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, whereas system acceptance was examined through a User Acceptance Test. The strongest reported result was obtained for employee-performance prediction, with 87.24% accuracy, 86% precision, 85% recall, and 85.5% F1-score. Feature-importance analysis as the explainable artificial intelligence component identified performance score, competency level, and years of service as the three most influential variables. The integrated dashboard and AI Assistant provided consolidated access to analytical information, and the UAT result reached 91.40%. Overall, the findings suggest that SIPINTAR can move personnel information management beyond historical record keeping toward predictive and explainable decision support. Nevertheless, the results should be validated with baseline models and broader institutional datasets before being generalized across agencies.

items.abstract: The purpose of this review is to examine the diagnostic challenges arising from the mathematical biases of the DAS28 index used in monitoring rheumatoid arthritis, as well as the psychological and neurobiological factors underlying patient-physician discordance. Furthermore, this paper aims to analyze the role of digital biomarkers in future decision-making. A structural characteristic of the DAS28 index is that its subjective components carry twice the weight of objective metrics. In cases of central sensitization, depression, or anxiety, this can result in "false-positive" disease activity, leading to unjustified and costly interventions, as well as ineffective therapy. Literature confirms that patient-physician discordance is one of the primary predictors of therapeutic failure, particularly in difficult-to-treat (D2T) cases. The application of the DAS28-P index can help identify pain-dominant phenotypes. Besides musculoskeletal ultrasound, new technologies, such as keystroke dynamics analysis or artificial intelligence-based imaging, offer objective measures to eliminate subjective biases. Modern rheumatological approaches should integrate psychological support, patient education, and pain modulation alongside immunosuppressive treatment. The implementation of digital biomarkers and hybrid care models not only improves the patient's quality of life but also generates significant system-level cost savings in healthcare. items.title: A Survey of Agentic AI: Architectures, Reasoning, Planning, Memory, Collaboration, and Real-World Applications
items.abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a new paradigm that allows intelligent systems to behave independently, pursue specific objectives, and adapt to changing circumstances. Agentic AI combines reasoning, planning, memory, learning, and tool utilization to do complicated tasks with minimal human involvement, in contrast to traditional AI systems that mainly react to user inputs. In this article, takes a look at Agentic AI from every angle: its theoretical underpinnings, technological supports, architectural blueprints, and real-world uses. Many models and frameworks are covered, including cognitive and modular designs, systems based on reinforcement learning, hybrid models, and multi-agent systems. Symbolic, probabilistic, and self-reflective reasoning are some of the reasoning methodologies covered. Classical, hierarchical, and adaptive planning strategies are also covered. Agents' ability to reliably and efficiently execute tasks is investigated by looking at memory management, communication protocols, coordination mechanisms, and collaborative decision-making. A wide range of business, medical, financial, academic, and personal aid apps are evaluated in the poll. Privacy, security, computational costs, scalability, and unexpected behavior are the main issues that are highlighted in the end. The study emphasizes the need for more investigation into how to create Agentic AI systems that are reliable, flexible, and effective.

items.title: Abdurauf Fitrat's term-formation principles and the semantic-functional adaptation of artificial intelligence terms into Uzbek
items.abstract: This article compares Abdurauf Fitrat’s principles of terminology formation with contemporary strategies for adapting English artificial intelligence terminology into Uzbek. Its objective is to develop qualitative criteria for evaluating terminological equivalents in relation to meaning, linguistic structure, and communicative use. The material comprises seven selected expressions: artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, neural network, prompt, chatbot, and large language model. Comparative, componential, word formation, and functional pragmatic methods are employed. The analysis distinguishes calquing, direct borrowing, hybrid nomination, and descriptive rendering. It shows that formal similarity to an English source expression does not necessarily guarantee conceptual accuracy or accessibility for readers. The interpretation of prompt depends on context. Fitrat’s linguistic legacy is treated as a historical comparative perspective rather than direct evidence of continuity with digital terminology. A four criterion assessment framework is proposed, covering conceptual precision, structural compatibility, communicative transparency, and terminological consistency. These qualitative conclusions require corpus verification. The framework may inform terminology development.

items.title: ADOPTION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: BARRIERS AND ENABLERS IN DEVELOPING ECONOMIES
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology capable of enhancing efficiency, decision-making, and resilience in supply chain management. However, its adoption in developing economies remains constrained by several technological, organizational, and environmental challenges. This study examined the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management, with emphasis on the barriers and enablers in developing economies, using Nigeria as the study context. A cross-sectional survey research design was adopted, and data were collected from 235 employees, managers, and supply chain professionals in selected manufacturing firms, logistics companies, retail organizations, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria using a structured questionnaire titled Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Supply Chain Management Index (AIASCMI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson Product Moment Correlation. The findings revealed that identified barriers, including inadequate digital infrastructure, high implementation costs, shortage of skilled personnel, and organizational challenges, have a significant negative relationship with the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. The study also found that identified enablers, such as top management support, technological readiness, employee competence, and government support, significantly influence the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence. The study concludes that overcoming existing barriers while strengthening organizational and technological capabilities is essential for the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. It is recommended that organizations invest in digital infrastructure, workforce development, and supportive management practices to maximize the benefits of Artificial Intelligence and improve supply chain performance.

items.title: ADOPTION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: BARRIERS AND ENABLERS IN DEVELOPING ECONOMIES
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology capable of enhancing efficiency, decision-making, and resilience in supply chain management. However, its adoption in developing economies remains constrained by several technological, organizational, and environmental challenges. This study examined the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management, with emphasis on the barriers and enablers in developing economies, using Nigeria as the study context. A cross-sectional survey research design was adopted, and data were collected from 235 employees, managers, and supply chain professionals in selected manufacturing firms, logistics companies, retail organizations, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria using a structured questionnaire titled Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Supply Chain Management Index (AIASCMI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson Product Moment Correlation. The findings revealed that identified barriers, including inadequate digital infrastructure, high implementation costs, shortage of skilled personnel, and organizational challenges, have a significant negative relationship with the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. The study also found that identified enablers, such as top management support, technological readiness, employee competence, and government support, significantly influence the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence. The study concludes that overcoming existing barriers while strengthening organizational and technological capabilities is essential for the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. It is recommended that organizations invest in digital infrastructure, workforce development, and supportive management practices to maximize the benefits of Artificial Intelligence and improve supply chain performance.

items.title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence as a Digital Employee: Redefining the Boundaries of Delegation, Accountability, and Control in Information Systems-Enabled Organizations
items.abstract: Background and Purpose: The rapid transition from deterministic automation and passive algorithmic decision-support systems to agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) represents an unprecedented ontological shift in enterprise information systems (IS). Unlike antecedent generative models that merely synthesize conversational text, agentic AI operates with persistent internal memory, autonomous multi-step cognitive reasoning, goal decomposition, and self-directed tool and API execution. In contemporary digital organizations, these autonomous systems are progressively onboarded, provisioned, and treated not merely as passive software artifacts, but as synthetic workers or "digital employees." However, this conceptual elevation fractures foundational organizational assumptions rooted in classical agency theory, sociotechnical systems theory, and managerial control architectures. This monograph investigates how enterprise deployment of digital employees redefines the boundaries of delegation, moral and organizational accountability, and managerial control within IS-enabled organizational environments. Design, Methodology, and Approach: To rigorously interrogate this emergent socio-algorithmic reality, an extensive explanatory mixed-methods research design was executed across a 24-month longitudinal investigation (2024-2026). The quantitative phase collected and analyzed empirical survey data from 482 senior enterprise leaders, Chief Information Officers (CIOs), Chief AI Officers (CAIOs), Enterprise Architects, and line managers across four knowledge-intensive industry verticals (Financial Services & FinTech, Healthcare & HealthTech, Global Supply Chain Logistics, and Enterprise Cloud/SaaS). Structural Equation Modeling using Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM) was employed to empirically test the structural dependencies between perceived agentic autonomy, algorithmic trust, delegation depth, operational agility, and accountability drift. The qualitative phase comprised 38 semi-structured, in-depth key-informant interviews and four comprehensive, longitudinal multi-case studies examining end-to-end organizational deployments of multi-agent architectures (including LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, and proprietary enterprise agent meshes). Rigorous thematic analysis and qualitative comparative synthesis were conducted to deconstruct operational failures, behavioral drift phenomena, and governance adaptations. Empirical Findings: The empirical results reveal a profound structural paradox in enterprise agentic delegation. First, the transition from "task offloading" to "autonomous mandate delegation" generates a statistically significant positive effect on organizational agility (β=0.495, p<0.001) and operational velocity, but concurrently fuels a critical "accountability void" and organizational drift (β=0.342, p<0.001). Second, traditional managerial control frameworks specifically diagnostic and boundary controls suffer severe operational degradation when confronted with non-deterministic agentic planning and recursive API invocation. Third, human supervisors frequently exhibit either "cognitive abandonment" (over-trusting autonomous agents due to perceived competence) or severe "algorithmic cynicism" (resorting to micro-surveillance that negates agentic throughput benefits). Fourth, the investigation reveals the emergence of what we conceptualize as the "Synthetic Moral Crumple Zone," wherein middle-tier human managers are held legally and administratively accountable for unforeseen agentic systemic errors that they possessed neither the technical visibility nor the temporal window to prevent.

items.title: AI and the Shift in Power Dynamics in English Language Education: Portfolios as Tools for Authentic Self-Agency and Self-Determination
items.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in English language education is reshaping traditional pedagogical frameworks, fostering learner autonomy, and redefining the educator’s role. This article presents a conceptual framework and pedagogical model exploring how AI-driven portfolio assessment and custom AI language models can be integrated within an Agile learning framework to support iterative, self-directed learning. While AI enhances language acquisition through personalized feedback and adaptive learning, concerns about authenticity, plagiarism, and over-reliance on AI-generated content remain. A structured approach to AI literacy development is introduced, ensuring that students critically assess AI-generated feedback rather than passively accepting it. A key component of this framework is AI-supported reflection, where learners evaluate AI suggestions based on alignment with their authentic voice and intended meaning. This process is reinforced through an AI-reflection rubric designed to cultivate metacognitive awareness and critical engagement with AI outputs. Agile methodologies, particularly iterative learning cycles, scaffold AI-supported writing assignments, balancing human and AI feedback for progressive skill development. The article also examines configurable AI tools for assessment, such as custom GPTs within ChatGPT and Gems within Google Gemini, which can evaluate language proficiency, track learning progression, and facilitate AI-supported peer assessment. The framework is designed to be adaptable across international EFL and ESL contexts, supporting authentic learning rather than replacing the learner’s central role in the learning process.

items.title: AI CHAT ASSISTANT FOR ONLINE BUSINESS
items.abstract: Online businesses must answer product questions, explain policies, guide purchases and resolve order-related concerns across multiplechannels. Human-only support can be costly and slow during peak demand, while rigid rule-based chatbots struggle with varied wording andmulti-step questions. This paper presents a conceptual design for an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chat Assistant for Online Business thatcombines natural language understanding, retrieval from approved business knowledge, controlled access to commerce services andescalation to human staff. The proposed assistant interprets customer intent, retrieves relevant product and policy information, generatesgrounded responses, and invokes permitted actions such as checking order status only after appropriate authentication. The architectureemphasizes factual consistency, privacy, security, accessibility and measurable service quality. It also describes a developmentmethodology, evaluation metrics, risk controls and a staged deployment plan. Since this is a design-oriented study, no original performanceresults are claimed; the proposed evaluation must be conducted using representative customer queries and verified business data.

items.title: AI DRIVEN DIGITAL TWINS FOR DRUG REPURPOSING: CURRENT EVIDENCES, APPLICATIONS, TRANSLATIONAL CHALLENGES AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
items.abstract: Conventional drug discovery and development is associated with substantial financial costs, lengthy development timelines, and high attrition rates during preclinical and clinical evaluation. Drug repurposing provides an alternative strategy by identifying new therapeutic applications for existing drugs with previously characterized pharmacological and safety profiles. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, multimodal biomedical data integration, mechanistic modelling, and digital twin technology have created new opportunities to improve computational drug repurposing and patient-specific treatment prediction. This review examines the emerging integration of AI-driven digital twins with drug repurposing, focusing on digital twin architectures, artificial intelligence methodologies multi modal data integration, drug target prediction, pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic modelling, treatment-response simulation, and personalized therapeutic decision-making. The review also discusses applications across cancer, neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, infectious, metabolic, and rare diseases. Particular emphasis is placed on the development of patient-specific digital twins, integration of multi-omics and clinical data, virtual treatment simulation, and validation through computational, experimental, and clinical approaches. Major challenges include data heterogeneity, interoperability, model reliability, uncertainty quantification, interpretability, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, privacy, clinical workflow integration, and regulatory acceptance. Emerging approaches, including causal AI, federated learning, multimodal foundation models, virtual clinical trials, and real-time adaptive digital twins, may further enhance the translational potential of AI-enabled drug repurposing. However, prospective clinical validation and standardized regulatory frameworks remain necessary before widespread clinical implementation.

items.title: AI Governance In India: A Critical Examination Of Digital Rights, Constitutional Safeguards And Legal Accountability
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence currently determines how individuals access information, services and decisions from institutions. The influence of this technology raises questions about how the law can hold those who control such power accountable under the constitution. In this article I investigate if the developing governance framework in India protects digital rights and offers ways to fix harm caused by artificial intelligence. It applies to a qualitative doctrinal method to examine constitutional guarantees, court decisions, laws plus official policies. To assist this analysis, the text includes a comparison of two international instruments. The discussion distinguishes between constitutional duties, laws that the state has passed but not fully started, secondary regulations and governance principles that lack binding force. I argue that protecting privacy does not solve the problems of unfair classification, hidden decision processes, or deception. Privacy laws do not address how companies spread responsibility across long supply chains. India uses a strategy that focuses on innovation and treats different industries separately - this method is flexible, but it is only legitimate if the state provides rules for fair procedures but also ways for citizens to complain. In response, I propose a framework for constitutional accountability - this framework connects the requirement for a legal basis, the balance of interests, equal treatment and clear explanations. It also requires that a human reviews decisions and that victims receive a fix for their injuries. The specific recommendations include tests to see how important uses of technology affect society. There must be records that allow independent experts to check the system. On top of this the state must use safeguards when it buys technology. Responsibility is assigned to the party who controls risks that they can predict.

items.title: AI Governance: What Exactly Are We Governing?
items.abstract: WP_AI_8.5 develops a three-object framework for clarifying what AI governance is actually governing. The paper begins from a structural problem in contemporary AI governance. Technical systems, human decision-makers, institutional actors, oversight mechanisms, accountability, safety, and responsibility are often discussed within the same governance language without clearly separating the objects to which those rules apply. This can produce governance object drift, in which the focus of governance shifts during analysis, and governance subject inversion, in which AI becomes increasingly personalized as the apparent actor while the humans and institutions exercising real authority become less visible. The paper identifies three distinct but connected objects of AI governance. The first is the AI entity itself. The paper distinguishes four governance identities: Tool, System, Agent, and Autonomous Actor. These categories are not claims about consciousness or legal personhood. They describe different operational relationships between AI capability, delegated authority, persistence, external consequence, and human reauthorization. The second object is the human authority structure across the AI lifecycle. Developers, testers, providers, approvers, regulators, administrators, operators, and users exercise different forms of authority and therefore require different forms of governance. Human conduct must remain a direct object of AI governance rather than being displaced by anthropomorphic descriptions of AI behavior. The third object is the institutional interface through which AI capability enters society. Admission, authorization, release, deployment, access, supervision, review, restriction, suspension, and withdrawal determine how technical capability becomes socially operative. The paper also distinguishes Governance Identity Drift from Governance Object Drift. The former occurs when an AI system’s actual operational identity changes while its formal governance category remains unchanged. The latter occurs when governance itself shifts its analytical object, for example when a human authorization decision is gradually redescribed as autonomous machine behavior. The central argument is that governance must define its own objects rather than inherit them passively from technical narratives. AI should be governed according to what kind of operational entity it is. Humans and institutions should be governed according to the authority they exercise. The human-AI institutional interface should be governed according to the social consequences it enables. WP_AI_8.5 builds on the preceding papers in the WP_AI_8 series. WP_AI_8.1 established the engineering circuit-breaker principle; WP_AI_8.2 examined responsibility escape; WP_AI_8.3 developed a dual-track framework connecting capability control and human responsibility; and WP_AI_8.4 addressed the conditions under which AI capability may move from controlled development into social release. WP_AI_8.5 moves one level upward by clarifying the governance objects to which those mechanisms apply.

items.title: AI in HRM: a unified model of AI capabilities and process efficiency for enhanced HRM effectiveness
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming human resource management (HRM) by supporting recruitment, training, performance management, workforce planning, talent analytics, and employee engagement. Nevertheless, limited evidence explains how different AI-enabled HRM practices contribute to process efficiency, decision-making, workforce agility, and overall HRM effectiveness. This study examined six AI-enabled HRM capabilities through an integrated Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory framework. The proposed model included AI in Recruitment and Selection, Training and Development, Performance Management, Strategic HR Planning, Talent Analytics and Retention, and Employee Engagement and Wellbeing. HR Process Efficiency, Decision-Making Accuracy, and Workforce Agility and Innovation were examined as organizational mechanisms contributing to Enhanced HRM Effectiveness. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 256 h professionals from public-sector, private-sector, and higher-education settings in Saudi Arabia and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The findings showed that recruitment and performance-management AI were positively associated with HR process efficiency, while strategic-planning and talent-analytics AI were positively associated with decision-making accuracy. Employee engagement and wellbeing AI was positively associated with workforce agility and innovation. However, training and development AI was not significantly associated with process efficiency, and decision-making accuracy was not significantly associated with enhanced HRM effectiveness. The study demonstrates that the contribution of AI to HRM effectiveness depends on the HR function and the organizational mechanism involved. The findings provide theoretical and practical guidance for integrating AI with HR expertise, organizational routines, workforce capabilities, and responsible governance.

items.title: AI in mathematics classrooms: a synergistic strategy for diversity and inclusivity
items.abstract: Despite growing emphasis on inclusive education, mathematics classrooms still exhibit disparities arising from cognitive, linguistic, socioeconomic, and systemic barriers, marginalizing diverse students and limiting equitable learning opportunities. Artificial intelligence (AI) presents considerable potential for addressing these challenges. This study investigates how AI technologies can be harnessed to create mathematics classrooms that are inclusive and adaptive to individual student needs. Anchored in Universal Design for Learning (UDL) and the Substitution, Augmentation, Modification, Redefinition (SAMR) frameworks, the study explores how AI functionalities can facilitate personalized learning, responsive instruction, and equitable participation. The study employs a hybrid conceptual–structured narrative review approach, synthesizing existing literature through structured searching, screening, thematic coding, and conceptual integration. The synthesis examines AI functionalities, inclusive pedagogical affordances, implementation challenges, ethical and equity concerns, and future directions. On this basis, the study develops the Synergistic AI-Inclusive Mathematics Education (SAIME) framework, conceptualizing UDL as an inclusion-oriented design foundation, SAMR as a technological transformation pathway, and teacher-mediated pedagogy and ethical safeguards as essential conditions for equitable outcomes in access, participation, and achievement. It concludes that AI can contribute meaningfully to inclusive mathematics education when its technological affordances are purposefully aligned with inclusive pedagogy, ethical and equity safeguards, and equitable learning goals.

items.title: AI Redefines Next-Gen Drilling Vibration Compliance
items.abstract: _ This case study from Tomax outlines the use of artificial intelligence to analyze high-fidelity data of the full drilling process. The problem of downhole vibrations remains a significant barrier for the drilling industry. An emerging technology based on direct interception of disturbing resonances is now being used to address the issue. Such solutions rely on a new level of understanding with respect to the true bottomhole assembly (BHA) dynamics. Artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) techniques are now helping deliver the full picture. While the specific product development in this field belongs in the commercial space, the necessity for more and better data on drilling dynamics is commonplace. This case study describes a successful solution for data harvesting on a level that is both new and found to meet requirement for the application of AI/ML solutions. The study concludes with examples from analysis that reveal the potential from a true image of everything going on in a drillstring. Reinventing Drilling Dynamics Traditional analysis of drilling dynamics frequently references data from downhole accelerometers. However, these systems typically capture a mix of effects rather than the underlying coupling of forces that cause resonances and, consequently, poor performance and downtime from failures. The fundamentals of these resonances reside in the transfer of torsional and axial forces from surface to the bit. On most rigs, the surface input and reactive loads are recorded at sparse intervals (typically every 10 seconds or longer). Capturing this critical information at a high-fidelity level in this environment presents two critical challenges: - Signal Integrity: Eliminating data corruption and packet loss from intermittent transfer when sampling frequencies exceeding 1,000 Hz using RF from a rotating shaft in a rough environment. - Data Pipeline: While modern sensor assemblies can export structural acoustics and stress waves at extreme sample rates, the bottleneck is the data pipeline and the requirement for a continuous stream of megabytes of time-stamped data every second into a usable database.

items.title: AI-ASSISTED UV–VISIBLE SPECTROSCOPY FOR RAPID QUANTIFICATION OF PHARMACEUTICAL DRUGS
items.abstract: UV–Visible (UV–Vis) spectrophotometry is a rapid, economical and widely available technique for pharmaceutical analysis, but its selectivity is limited when the drugs in a formulation have overlapping absorption spectra. The integration of chemometrics and artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML) algorithms such as partial least squares (PLS), principal component regression (PCR), support vector regression (SVR), artificial neural networks (ANN) and random forests, with intelligent wavelength selection and metaheuristic optimization (genetic and Firefly algorithms), allows the simultaneous quantification of several active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) from the whole spectrum rather than a single wavelength. This review summarizes the principles of UV–Vis spectroscopy, the current status of AI-assisted UV–Vis analysis, and the challenges related to model interpretability, data integrity, validation and instrument variability. Applications, drawbacks and futureprospects are discussed, including process analytical technology (PAT), portable instruments, green analytical chemistry and regulatory acceptance of AI-enabled spectroscopic methods as complementary tools to chromatographic assays in pharmaceutical quality control.

items.abstract: Software development often requires programmers to write repetitive code, understand unfamiliar requirements, and spend considerabletime identifying and correcting errors. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have enabled systems to generate source code fromnatural-language instructions. However, generated code may contain syntax errors, incorrect logic, insecure patterns, or incompletehandling of edge cases. This paper proposes an AI-Based Code Generation and Self-Testing System that accepts a programming task innatural language, generates a candidate solution, prepares or selects test cases, executes the code in a controlled environment, and analysesthe results. The proposed workflow combines prompt interpretation, code generation, static validation, test-case generation, sandboxedexecution, and feedback-based refinement. The system is intended to support developers and learners by reducing repetitive effort andproviding an initial validation cycle. It does not replace code review or guarantee correctness; execution safety, test coverage, modellimitations, and human verification remain important. This paper presents a proposed methodology and evaluation plan. Quantitativeperformance claims should be added only after implementation and testing.

items.title: AI-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality–Emotional Attachment–Loyalty Pathway in 2025–2026
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although online-shopping participation should not be interpreted as a direct measure of AI adoption or retailer-specific investment. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). The study considers a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents (β = 0.289, p = 0.001) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents (β = −0.023, p = 0.811). Age-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51.2% of the variance in loyalty (R2 = 0.512) and has positive predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.289). Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty.
